literal: Even if others do improper things to oneself, feeling pain and not doing unvirtuous things is good.
translation: Even if others do improper and harmful things to you, it is best to feel pity for the pain they might suffer and refrain from doing anything unvirtuous in return.
modern: தமக்குத் தகுதியில்லாத தீமைகளைப் பிறர் செய்தாலும், அதனால் வரும் துன்பத்திற்கு வருந்தி, அறமல்லாத செயல்களை அவர்களுக்குச் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதே நல்லது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the peak of patience and forbearance. When others do improper or harmful things (tiṟaṉalla) to us, our natural reaction might be revenge. However, the poet advises us to feel pity or sorrow (nō nōntu) for the pain or consequences that the wrongdoer might face, and to absolutely refrain from returning unvirtuous deeds (aṟaṉalla ceyyāmai). By choosing not to retaliate, we preserve our own virtue and demonstrate true strength of character.
